translationRepairs: Chinese annotation brackets 〈〉 enclose the parenthetical note; English already uses ASCII parentheses, so the leftover fullwidth 〉 is a stray artifact with no semantic role.
Same stray fullwidth 〉 as in the idiomatic field; the Chinese closes with annotation bracket 〉 already mirrored by English ), so removing the leftover character is correct.
When the Last Emperor took the throne, he became prefect of Pu, then of Cao.
When the Last Emperor took the throne, he became prefect of Pu, then of Chan.
Focus unit has 澶州刺史; 澶 is Chan (Danzhou), whereas Cao would be 曹. Replacing Cao with Chan restores the prefecture correctly.
When the Last Emperor acceded, he was moved to prefect of Pu, then transferred to prefect of Cao.
When the Last Emperor acceded, he was moved to prefect of Pu, then transferred to prefect of Chan.
Literal likewise mistranslates 澶州 as Cao; Chan matches 澶 and distinguishes it from 曹州.
Jin took Cao Prefecture, carried Yanzhang’s family to Taiyuan, gave them a mansion and rich provision, and sent envoys now and then to win him over. Yanzhang killed every envoy and broke for good.
Jin took Chan Prefecture, carried Yanzhang’s family to Taiyuan, gave them a mansion and rich provision, and sent envoys now and then to win him over. Yanzhang killed every envoy and broke for good.
晉軍攻破澶州 names Chan Prefecture again; Cao is the wrong place-name and the rest of the sentence is otherwise faithful.

The Jin army took Cao Prefecture, carried off Yanzhang’s wife and children to Taiyuan, granted them a mansion, and supplied them generously. From time to time they sent envoys to win Yanzhang over; Yanzhang executed the envoys to cut himself off.

The Jin army took Chan Prefecture, carried off Yanzhang’s wife and children to Taiyuan, granted them a mansion, and supplied them generously. From time to time they sent envoys to win Yanzhang over; Yanzhang executed the envoys to cut himself off.
Literal repeats the 澶州→Cao error; Chan is the accurate English for 澶州 and leaves the capture and embassy wording intact.
He then made Renzhan Acting Grand Preceptor of War, Central Secretariat Director, and Military Governor of Pingyi.
He then made Renzhan Acting Grand Commandant and Concurrent Director of the Secretariat, and Military Governor of the Tianping Army.
檢校太尉兼中書令 is Acting Grand Commandant and Concurrent Director of the Secretariat (太尉≠太師); 天平軍節度使 is Military Governor of the Tianping Army, not Pingyi.
He then appointed Renzhan Acting Grand Preceptor of War and Concurrent Central Secretariat Director and Military Governor of Pingyi.
He then appointed Renzhan Acting Grand Commandant and Concurrent Director of the Secretariat and Military Governor of the Tianping Army.
Same office errors in the literal: 太尉→Grand Commandant and 天平軍→Tianping Army; the proposed wording restores both titles without inventing content.
